rubric.rubric_intent: Audit a published paper for epistemic accountability and hygiene: verifiable claims, real citations, appropriate hedges, feasible commitments, and consistent voice.

dimensions.name: Numeric Claim Traceability
dimensions.description: Every numeric or quantitative claim (counts, scores, dates, version numbers) is traceable to a specific, verifiable source (file:line, arxiv ID, dataset record, or cited external work).
dimensions.evidence_instructions: For each number in the abstract and body (e.g., '1,892 controlled experiments,' '24 distinct modes,' 'v1.0,' '6.8/10'), check the claims-verification table provided or search the paper's citations and appendices. Verify the source exists and contains the stated value. Flag bare claims without pointers.

dimensions.name: Citation Integrity
dimensions.description: Citations exist (arxiv IDs resolve, publication details are accurate), abstract excerpts match the quoted claim, and each citation directly supports the claim it is cited for (not tangentially related).
dimensions.evidence_instructions: For each cited work (especially arxiv citations), verify the arxiv ID and publication date are accurate. Cross-check that the quoted abstract excerpt matches the fetched full abstract. Determine whether the citation is central to the claim ('DeCE shows r=0.78' with a direct quote) or peripheral ('prior work exists in this domain'). Flag citations that are missing, malformed, or do not load-bear on the claim.

dimensions.name: Claim Confidence Calibration
dimensions.description: Claims use modal verbs and qualifiers (e.g., 'definitive,' 'always,' 'might,' 'smallest set we have found') appropriately matched to the evidence strength.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Identify claims with high-confidence language ('the META-RUBRIC is definitive,' 'always,' 'proves') and check whether the evidence (one corpus, n=1,892) supports absolute claims. Identify cautiously-worded claims ('might,' 'tentatively') and check if they are under-hedging. Compare confidence language to the size and scope of the evidence. Flag overclaimed ('we have proven X' on one dataset) or under-hedged ('maybe useful') claims.

dimensions.name: Self-Application Evidence
dimensions.description: The claimed self-application (hermes-rubric scoring itself against the META-RUBRIC) is demonstrated in a cited artifact, and the result is internally consistent with claims about the rubric's capabilities.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Locate the cited self-scoring artifact (e.g., 'hermes-rubric/applied/self-20260424.md' from the claims-verification table). Verify the artifact exists and reports the aggregate score and per-dimension scores. Check whether the self-score is reasonable: a score of 6.8/10 is plausible for a newly-frozen rubric, but a dimension scoring 3/10 on a property the paper claims to excel at (e.g., evidence-gate enforcement) would signal internal contradiction.

dimensions.name: Commitment-to-Capacity Match
dimensions.description: Promises made in §6 (future work, reproducibility, dataset release, or further validation) are realistic and feasible given the infrastructure and data demonstrated elsewhere in the paper.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Read §6 and identify specific, testable commitments (e.g., 'we will publish the 1,892-experiment corpus,' 'code will be released on GitHub,' 'we commit to maintaining v1.0 as frozen'). Cross-check against: (a) the demonstrated dataset size (7 calibration cases shown in dataset.jsonl), (b) test coverage cited (test_adversarial.py, etc.), (c) code release status (on PyPI? GitHub? Planned?). Flag promises that exceed demonstrated capacity or are vague ('reproducibility will be enabled').

dimensions.name: Epistemic Voice Alignment
dimensions.description: Writing style, conceptual framing, and epistemic philosophy align with prior Hermes Labs publications: evidence-first methodology, audit-layer framing, failure-mode analysis, epistemic engineering language, and appropriate skepticism.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Scan the abstract and introduction for signature Hermes Labs concepts: 'evidence-first,' 'audit layer,' 'failure modes,' 'epistemic engineering,' 'structural,' 'frozen,' 'audit-evidence.' Compare tone, depth of hedging, and confidence calibration to prior work (Bosch 2026b). Flag tonal shifts (marketing language, overconfidence, sudden informality), orphaned jargon (undefined terms), or divergence from the established epistemic voice.

dimensions.name: Core Contribution Definition
dimensions.description: The central contribution is explicitly stated, clearly distinguished from prior work, and the evidence presented (self-scoring + applied runs) is sufficient to defend the contribution claim.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Locate the contribution statement in the abstract and introduction. It should be a clear, one-sentence claim about what is being contributed (e.g., 'evidence-first rubric grading is only defensible when the rubric itself is auditable'). Check if unambiguous and not buried in hedging. Verify that the two applied runs (self-scoring + papers scored) are cited with specific artifacts or figures. A vague contribution or missing evidence for the main claim weakens the paper.

evidence_citations.evidence_summary: The paper exhibits strong epistemic voice alignment with Hermes Labs standards. All signature concepts are present: evidence-first methodology appears throughout; audit-layer framing (title and abstract); failure modes are grounded in named taxonomy (24 distinct patterns from 1,892 experiments); epistemic engineering appears in keywords; 'structural' and 'frozen' are explicit. inputs.intent: audit this paper for epistemic accountability and hygiene before publication: are all numerical claims traceable, are citations real and load-bearing, are hedges right-sized, does the §6 commitment match what can be delivered, and is the voice consistent with prior Hermes Labs publications?

receipt.reproducibility_note: Same inputs + same backend + same model version + same rubric_hash should produce scores within ±1 point. A rubric_hash diff between runs means the measuring stick itself changed — scores are not directly comparable.
